We have used pesticides and herbicides in farming for many, many generations - and, more recently, these methods have improved. Genetic modification isn't bad, in and of itself. Tilling isn't bad, though it can be overdone and some soils aren't best suited for it. Pesticides and herbicides can be applied in isolation - and that's even more likely as they work to modify robots which can tend and spot apply the two.

You're best choice is to start with a State coop or the agriculture extension at your local university. My berries are wild Maine blueberries and a very different species than you'd be considering. None of my knowledge will help you and would only serve to confuse you.

You'll want a cultivar that's hardy in your growing environment and suitable to your soil types. The plants you'll want will be high bush berries which are easily harvested by hand picking. Mine are low bush and use a timed device called a rake to be harvested.

Your local university will probably have an agricultural extension, though you can Google for associations and berry co-ops, or the likes. They will be able to get you started with information that is valid for your area.

Mine just grow naturally. I burn the field every other year, spot spray, and dust by plane. We put hay on them after harvest and, come spring, we set that fucker ablaze and party around the fire. You almost certainly won't be doing it that way.
